transcript: Last night, I saw The Ally at The Public. In his new play by Itamar Moses, a college professor named Asaf who considers himself atheist, Jewish, and progressive, grapples with conflicting ideas within communities which he has allegiances to. It’s messy, it's heavy, and arguably it's a bit much for a play. There are direct discussions of really potent and timely subjects, like police violence, systemic racism, and the Israel Palestine conflict. The writing, which is really impressive, is at the forefront here, leaving plot on the sidelines a bit. Each character is distinct from one another, but somewhat archetypal in order to neatly set up different points of view that Asaf has to navigate, and I think it wasn't really until act two where I felt like we had had enough time with the characters to make them feel like characters and not just devices for ideas. Overall, I felt like this play was more idea heavy than drama, but that doesn't mean that you won't feel anything if you see this. In fact, the play for some might be too close for comfort and it could definitely be triggering. And I think this play is meant to be experienced in many different ways so I can only really speak for myself in that regard. If this interests you, The Ally is currently running until early April. With that, another playbill for my collection.
